pr.title: Proactively update coroutine drop shim's phase to account for later passes applied during shim query
pr.description:
See comments in the pass and on test. Also see https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/137264#issuecomment-2669706718.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/137243
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/139698

r? scottmcm
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: No source-grounded original/transformed function pair can demonstrate this PR as a runtime value difference. The only historical change is compiler-internal state metadata: setting `body.phase = MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)` on a coroutine drop shim. The incorrect variant merely leaves that phase stale (`Analysis(PostCleanup)`), which causes intra-pass MIR validation in the `mir_shims` query to ICE on a runtime-only construct such as a transmute. The added regression test is `//@ build-pass` with `-Zvalidate-mir`; it is not `run-pass`, and the generated shim's runtime behavior is unchanged. Thus the failure is a compile-time ICE, not an observable wrong program value. Constructing two Rust functions that return or simulate the phase/validation state would be a contrived reimplementation of compiler metadata rather than the historical semantic transformation, and the historically incorrect variant would not compile under the relevant compiler anyway, so it could not be executed under Miri as required. Therefore no valid counterexample pair exists within the task constraints.

analysis.originalLogic: In `create_coroutine_drop_shim`, the shim MIR body is built from the coroutine body, `body.source.instance = drop_instance;` is set, and the body is returned. The shim is conceptually produced at the analysis-to-runtime transition: "Creating a coroutine drop shim happens on `Analysis(PostCleanup) -> Runtime(Initial)`". However, the returned body's `body.phase` was left at its prior analysis-phase value because "the pass manager doesn't update the phase of the coroutine drop shim."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior is *not transforming* the drop shim's phase: the shim body keeps its stale analysis-phase marker (`Analysis(PostCleanup)`) even though its contents are in the runtime phase. Because "the pass manager neither optimizes nor updates the phase for drop shim bodies", the phase stays stale when the shim is later processed through the `mir_shims` query. The pass manager then runs intra-pass validation on the shim "before we've updated the phase of the body from analysis", causing an ICE (e.g., on a transmute in the shim body). The fix is the transformation `body.phase = MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial);`.
analysis.inputDomain: Coroutine (async/await) MIR in edition 2024 whose generated drop shim body contains operations that are valid in the runtime phase but invalid/stale under the analysis phase, e.g. a transmute in the drop shim. The regression input is an async block that captures and drops a `Drop` type across an await: `async { vec![async { HasDrop }.await]; }`, compiled with `-Zvalidate-mir` and `//@ build-pass`.
analysis.summary: Bug-fix PR: when building a coroutine drop shim, explicitly set the shim body's phase to `MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)` because the pass manager does not update the phase of drop shim bodies. Without this, the stale analysis phase makes intra-pass MIR validation in the `mir_shims` query ICE on runtime-only constructs such as a transmute in the shim body.
analysis.trigger: A coroutine drop shim is created and later queried via the `mir_shims` query; the shim body contains a runtime-phase-only construct (e.g. transmute). The pass manager neither optimizes nor updates the shim's phase, so intra-pass validation runs while the body still claims to be in `Analysis(PostCleanup)` instead of `Runtime(Initial)`.
preconditions: Compiling an async/await coroutine (edition 2024) that generates a coroutine drop shim
The drop shim is processed through the `mir_shims` query after creation
The shim body contains a construct only valid in the runtime phase (e.g. a transmute)
pitfalls: Assuming the pass manager updates the phase for drop shim bodies; it does not optimize or update their phase
Conflating the parent coroutine body's phase with the independently constructed drop shim body's phase
Forgetting that intra-pass validation runs before the body phase is updated from analysis, so validation can see a stale analysis phase
Fixing only the fixed implementation without recognizing the missing phase assignment as the historically incorrect transformation
analysis.testStrategy: Add a build-pass UI regression test under tests/ui/async-await with `-Zvalidate-mir` and `edition: 2024` that constructs an async block capturing a `Drop` type across an await (`struct HasDrop; impl Drop for HasDrop { fn drop(&mut self) {} }`, `async { vec![async { HasDrop }.await]; }`). A future agent can compare two programs differing only in whether the shim phase is set to `MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)`, checking that the phase-updating variant validates without an ICE. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed.
